Big Question
Today’s Wonder

Bedivere promises to throw Excalibur into the lake, and it takes him three trips. What makes a promise hard to keep?

🎯
Objectives
By the end of this lesson…
📖Reading: I will read Book Four, Chapter 3, “The Last Battle,” and the Epilogue, “Avalon.”
🧵Term: I will use a new term, resolution, to tell how the whole book ends.
🔤Words: I will learn five words: truce, mortal, brandished, barge, and endured.
🌫️Evidence: I will follow Bedivere on his three trips to the lake and name the ladies in the barge.
📝Writing: I will plan Quick Write 5: one knight, one late moment.

The Passing of Arthur
Alfred, Lord Tennyson (1869) · Idylls of the King · “Take Excalibur”
Arthur is speaking to Sir Bedivere; then Bedivere answers.
Thou therefore take my brand Excalibur, Which was my pride: for thou rememberest how In those old days, one summer noon, an arm Rose up from out the bosom of the lake, Clothed in white samite, mystic, wonderful, Holding the sword—and how I rowed across And took it, and have worn it, like a king; And, wheresoever I am sung or told In aftertime, this also shall be known: But now delay not: take Excalibur, And fling him far into the middle mere: Watch what thou seest, and lightly bring me word.” To him replied the bold Sir Bedivere: “It is not meet, Sir King, to leave thee thus, Aidless, alone, and smitten through the helm— A little thing may harm a wounded man; Yet I thy hest will all perform at full, Watch what I see, and lightly bring thee word.”
brand: sword · which was my pride: which I was proud of · bosom: the middle; here, the surface of the lake · samite: rich, heavy silk · mystic: holy and mysterious · aftertime: the future · mere: a lake · lightly: quickly · meet: right, fitting · aidless: without help · hest: command · perform at full: carry out completely

🔤 Words: The Sword Returns to the Lake
The other five of this week’s ten words. Tap a card to hear it.
truce
An agreement to stop fighting for a time.
“…he bade them take two priests with them and go to make a month’s truce with Sir Mordred.” Green, The Last Battle
mortal
Causing death. A mortal foe is an enemy to the death.
“The two knights became mortal foes.” An example, not a quote
brandished
Waved a weapon in the air.
“Three times it brandished the sword on high…” Green, The Last Battle
barge
A long, flat-bottomed boat.
“Then the barge floated away into the mist and was lost to sight.” Green, The Last Battle
endured
Lasted; kept going for a long time.
“…always the belief endured in Britain…” Green, Avalon

Professor Lovelore

Well done. Think about where everyone ends up. The king is carried away to Avalon. The queen becomes a nun. Bedivere becomes a monk, and Launcelot a friar. The last knights go on pilgrimage. Each thread is tied off. That is resolution.

You have read how the king was carried away. Now follow Bedivere to the lake.

Type your answers here. Your work is saved and goes into your Week 5 Work PDF. First, three questions about Chapter 3 and the Epilogue. Then plan your Quick Write.

Part 1Chapter ThinkingComplete sentences, with details from the text.
1. The night before the battle, Gawain comes to Arthur in a dream. What does he warn, and what does he advise Arthur to do?
2. Sir Lucan, badly hurt himself, helps carry the king to the chapel. What does Arthur say about Lucan, and what does it show about Arthur?
3. As the barge leaves, Arthur gives Bedivere one last job and one promise. What are they, and why do they matter to the rest of the story?
